State Environment Impact Assessment Authorities will be responsible for granting the clearances, enhancing efficiency. The change follows a draft notification issued earlier this year, highlighting the experience of state bodies.

items.title: Shree Cement targets 100 MT capacity in 3-4 years on India growth bet
items.summary: Shree Cement plans to expand its production capacity to over 100 million tonnes per annum within four years. The company aims for a growth rate of 9-10 percent, surpassing the industry average. They have announced significant investments in new plants across various states in India to support this expansion. Shree Cement is also growing its ready-mix concrete operations, planning to increase capacity significantly.

items.title: PNB needs Rs 5,000 crore extra provisions under ECL, CEO sees limited impact
items.summary: Punjab National Bank expects an additional provision of approximately Rs 5,000 crore due to ECL migration. They initially estimated higher but reduced the expected requirement based on digital assessments. The bank has created dedicated platforms for credit cards, supply chain management, and cash management services. These initiatives are expected to enhance the bank's non-interest income during challenging times.

items.title: ORN Ventures gears up for global travel business push with Rs 10,000 cr investment
items.summary: ORN Ventures intends to invest over Rs 10,000 crore globally to enhance travel infrastructure and operations. The company aims to deepen its presence in international markets while scaling its direct operator-to-consumer platform. Investments will focus on building physical infrastructure and transport operations across 50-60 countries. Additionally, ORN plans to expand its franchisee network to 100 cities within India.

items.title: Reliance Brands trims losses in FY26, adds Stella McCartney, Fabletics to portfolio
items.summary: Reliance Brands has reported a revenue increase of 3.77 percent to Rs 3,390.89 crore for FY26. The company narrowed its losses to Rs 137.04 crore, compared to Rs 233.79 crore the previous year. It expanded its portfolio by adding globally recognized brands like Stella McCartney and Kurt Geiger. RBL operates over 1,085 Points of Sale across India as of March 31, 2026.

items.title: Chalet Hotels plans Rs 3,500 crore capex in 3 years; Delhi airport hotel to open 200 rooms: CEO
items.summary: Chalet Hotels aims to invest Rs 3,500 crore in expanding its hospitality portfolio over the next three years. The company will increase the number of rooms at its Taj property at Delhi airport to nearly 200. Several other projects are underway, including a Ritz-Carlton in Hyderabad and Hyatt Regency in Airoli. The company is cautious about expanding its Athiva brand until financial viability is proven.

items.title: Govt tightens rules for oil, gas block extensions, seeks bigger profit share
items.summary: The Indian government has updated its production-sharing contracts policy for seven oil and gas blocks. Extensions may last until a field's economic life ends, subject to performance criteria. Contractors must apply two years before contracts expire and aid thorough audits of recoverable reserves. Increased government profit shares are mandated during the extended period of the contracts. The policy aims to ensure better returns and compliance from contractors while offering flexibility.

items.title: Government, corporate spending to sustain global growth in 2027 as inflation eases: JPMorgan
items.summary: Global economic growth is projected to be resilient in 2027 due to continued government investment and corporate spending. Investment in technology and recovery in consumer demand are expected to drive this growth forward. Corporate investment, especially in artificial intelligence, is noteworthy, with major firms planning significant expenditure. Inflation pressures are anticipated to ease, strengthening household spending. However, rising government borrowing and competition for capital may pose challenges for financial markets.

items.summary: Quantum computing firms are testing energy-grid optimization, solar materials and hydrogen catalysts as they pursue practical uses.
